To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) structural joins can be efficiently implemented in the presence of node numbering schemes and 2) the use of sibling pointers in the B+-tree based algorithms can further expedite the structural joins by a significant factor.

(i) B+-tree structural join is the most promising approach, (ii) sibling pointers can be added to improve performance, and (iii) R-tree structural join is a viable alternative, but not as efficient as B+-tree.

(a) B+-tree structural join algorithms can achieve a performance gain of up to 2 orders of magnitude over state of the art algorithms; (b) B+-tree algorithms with sibling pointers are more robust and can achieve an average improvement of 1 order of magnitude over state-of-the-art algorithms; and (c) R-trees are less robust and provide an average improvement of up to 3 orders of magnitude over the state-of-the-art.
